analysis:
Examined the ProviderLoop+Serve.swift head text and the ProviderLoop+StartupPreload.swift patch and base. The PR makes two changes. (1) In ProviderLoop+Serve.swift, shutdown now appends selectedModelRecovery.attempt?.task (line 486) to the preload tasks that are cancelled and awaited by waitForPreloads. The inline unload loop is replaced by unloadAllModelsForShutdown() (line 512). (2) In ProviderLoop+StartupPreload.swift, finishStartupPreload (~line 299) enqueues selected-model recovery for candidates left cold for memory or a slot. It does this only when the task is not cancelled, the loop is not shutting down, and startupPreloadStopRequested is false.

Security review: no attestation, key, or encryption paths changed. The registration attestation provider, the App Attest resume responder (fixed process X25519 key), the connection authorization clearing, and the APNs challenge handling are unchanged. These cover TB-002, TB-011 and T-053. Recovery loads reuse the existing load admission, which per the base was ensureModelLoaded with allowEviction false. No new inbound surface or coordinator-controlled input is added. The recovery loads local, already advertised models; the candidate lists come from the startup summary.

Remaining unverified contracts, since the bodies are outside the supplied evidence:
- enqueueSelectedModelRecovery and unloadAllModelsForShutdown (in ProviderLoop+SelectedModelRecovery and elsewhere). I could not check that the new shutdown helper retains the old semantics of waiting for modelsUnloading and looping until modelSlots is empty.
- That recovery cannot load a model after isShuttingDown is set, or race with the guard at line 439. A recovery task started after the preload cancellation snapshot (lines 484-492) could keep a model loaded (T-028/T-029 availability and residue). The cancel-and-wait at lines 484-492 covers the currently tracked attempt only.
- That recovery respects the retiring/failed-selftest refusal and advertised-set filters, so it cannot re-advertise a retired model (compare retireModelAfterFailedSelfTest).

No concrete regression is visible. Next review should read the SelectedModelRecovery and unloadAllModelsForShutdown sources.
